items.headline: Nasdaq falls 2.6% as Meta and Tesla slide; Dow flat
items.note: On Thursday the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.60% to 26,008.86 and the S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,663.43, while the Dow edged up 0.02% to 52,867.98. Meta dropped nearly 8% after its first cash outflow in over a decade due to AI spending, and Tesla fell 3.1% after cutting its 2026 capital spending plans.

items.headline: Traders pare bets on more Fed rate hikes
items.note: After the tech sell-off, a December hike is no longer fully priced in; the implied probability fell to 85%, and traders removed almost a full quarter-point hike expected for next year. Rate expectations drive stock valuations and borrowing costs.

items.headline: OpenAI's GPT models arrive on Google Cloud
items.note: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are in limited preview in Google Cloud's Model Garden, with general availability planned in a few weeks. Microsoft stays OpenAI's primary cloud partner. Companies can now use OpenAI models inside whichever cloud they already run.

items.headline: Meta's AI spending turns its cash flow negative
items.note: Meta reported its first cash outflow in more than a decade because of AI-related expenditures, and the stock fell nearly 8%. It shows how costly the AI buildout is, even for the biggest companies, and why investors now watch spending closely.

items.headline: More AI-linked layoffs: Cloudflare, Coinbase, Upwork
items.note: Fast Company's tracker says these firms cited AI as they cut jobs this week. For an intern hunter, it signals a cautious market, so polish your portfolio and apply early.

items.headline: Mamdani proposes rule forcing chatbots to hand off to humans
items.note: The city proposed requiring businesses to connect customers to a human quickly when a chatbot can't help. It's only a proposal so far, but it shows NYC moving to regulate AI products locally.

items.headline: Mamdani says feds have abdicated on AI, backs data center moratorium
items.note: At an Oct 19 event he urged New Yorkers to push back on AI and said he will ask Gov. Hochul to sign a broader data center moratorium bill. State and city rules could shape where AI companies build and hire.

learn.term: Capital spending (capex) and free cash flow
learn.explain: Capital expenditure, or capex, is money a company spends on long-lasting things like data centers, chips and equipment. Free cash flow is the cash left after paying for operations and capex. If capex is bigger than the cash the business brings in, free cash flow goes negative, meaning the company must use savings or borrow. That is what Reuters reported for Meta this week: AI spending pushed it into a cash outflow, and the stock fell nearly 8%. Investors like growth, but they want to see the spending eventually pay off.
learn.try: Look up the capex line in a big tech company's latest quarterly report.
